AC Bonus.description: A dwarven defender gains a dodge bonus to AC beginning at +1, which increases as he advances in level, reaching +4 at 10th level.

Damage Reduction.description: Starting at 6th level, a dwarven defender can absorb part of the impact from each attack. He ignores 3 points of damage from every hit he takes. At 10th level, this increases to 6/-. This reduction can bring damage down to 0 but never below 0; the defender does not gain hit points from absorbed damage.

Defensive Stance.description: A dwarven defender can plant himself in place and become an immovable bulwark. While holding this stance, he gains extraordinary resilience and power but is unable to leave the position he occupies. He receives +2 to Strength, +4 to Constitution, a +2 resistance bonus to all saving throws, and a +4 dodge bonus to AC. The Constitution increase grants additional hit points equal to 2 per level, though these are lost when the stance ends and Constitution returns to normal. Unlike temporary hit points, these bonus hit points are not depleted before regular hit points. During a defensive stance, the defender cannot employ any skill or ability that requires changing position, including Move Silently and Jump. The stance persists for a number of rounds equal to 3 + the character's enhanced Constitution modifier. The defender may choose to end the stance early. Once the stance concludes, the defender becomes fatigued and suffers a -2 penalty to Strength for the remainder of the encounter. The number of times per day the defender may enter this stance is determined by his class level. Activating the stance requires no time, but can only be done on the defender's own turn. For instance, a defender struck by an arrow outside his turn cannot activate the stance to benefit from the extra Constitution-based hit points.

Improved Uncanny Dodge.description: At 6th level, a dwarven defender becomes immune to flanking, as he can respond to attackers on all sides with equal effectiveness. This prevents rogues from using flanking to deliver sneak attacks against him. However, a rogue whose level exceeds the defender's by four or more can still flank him and apply sneak attack damage. If a character gains uncanny dodge from a second class such as rogue, he automatically obtains improved uncanny dodge, and the levels from those classes combine when determining the minimum rogue level needed to flank him.

Mobile Defense.description: At 8th level, a dwarven defender gains the ability to reposition slightly during a defensive stance. He may take a single 5-foot step per round while in the stance without forfeiting its benefits.

Trap Sense.description: At 4th level, a dwarven defender develops a heightened awareness of traps, granting a +1 bonus on Reflex saves against traps and a +1 dodge bonus to AC versus trap attacks. These bonuses increase to +2 at 8th level. They stack with any trap sense bonuses from other classes.

Uncanny Dodge.description: From 2nd level onward, a dwarven defender possesses an extraordinary capacity to sense threats before consciously perceiving them. He keeps his Dexterity bonus to AC (if any) even when flat-footed or targeted by an unseen attacker. He still forfeits this bonus if rendered immobile. If the character also obtains uncanny dodge from another class such as rogue, he automatically receives improved uncanny dodge instead.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: A dwarven defender has proficiency with all simple weapons, all martial weapons, every category of armor, and shields.

classFeatures.description: The dwarven defender receives a dodge bonus to Armor Class that starts at +1 and improves as the defender gains levels, until it reaches +4 at 10th level.
classFeatures.name: AC Bonus

classFeatures.description: When he needs to, a defender can become a stalwart bastion of defense. In this defensive stance, a defender gains phenomenal strength and durability, but he cannot move from the spot he is defending. He gains +2 to Strength, +4 to Constitution, a +2 resistance bonus on all saves, and a +4 dodge bonus to AC. The increase in Constitution increases the defender's hit points by 2 points per level, but these hit points go away at the end of the defensive stance when the Constitution score drops back 4 points. These extra hit points are not lost first the way temporary hit points are. While in a defensive stance, a defender cannot use skills or abilities that would require him to shift his position, such as Move Silently or Jump. A defensive stance lasts for a number of rounds equal to 3 + the character's (newly improved) Constitution modifier. A defender may end his defensive stance voluntarily prior to this limit. At the end of the defensive stance, the defender is winded and takes a ?2 penalty to Strength for the duration of that encounter. A defender can only use his defensive stance a certain number of times per day as determined by his level (). Using the defensive stance takes no time itself, but a defender can only do so during his action. (A defender can't, for example, use the stance when struck down by an arrow in order to get the extra hit points from the increased Constitution.)
classFeatures.name: Defensive Stance

classFeatures.description: Starting at 2nd level, a dwarven defender gains the extraordinary ability to react to danger before his senses would normally allow him to even be aware of it. At 2nd level and above, he retains his Dexterity bonus to AC (if any) regardless of being caught flat-footed or struck by an invisible attacker. (He still loses any Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized.) If a character gains uncanny dodge from a second class (such as rogue), the character automatically gains improved uncanny dodge.
classFeatures.name: Uncanny Dodge

classFeatures.description: At 4th level, a dwarven defender gains an intuitive sense that alerts him to danger from traps, giving him a +1 bonus on Reflex saves made to avoid traps and a +1 dodge bonus to AC against attacks by traps. At 8th level, these bonuses rise to +2. These bonuses stack with trap sense bonuses gained from other classes.
classFeatures.name: Trap Sense

classFeatures.description: At 6th level, a dwarven defender gains the ability to shrug off some amount of injury from each blow or attack. Subtract 3 points from the damage the dwarven defender takes each time he is dealt damage. At 10th level, this damage reduction rises to 6/?. Damage reduction can reduce damage to 0 but not below 0. (That is, the defender cannot actually gain hit points in this manner.)
classFeatures.name: Damage Reduction

classFeatures.description: At 6th level, a dwarven defender can no longer be flanked, since he can react to opponents on opposite sides of him as easily as he can react to a single attacker. This defense denies rogues the ability to use flank attacks to sneak attack the dwarven defender. The exception to this defense is that a rogue at least four levels higher than the dwarven defender can flank him (and thus sneak attack him). If a character gains uncanny dodge from a second class (such as rogue), the character automatically gains improved uncanny dodge, and the levels from those classes stack to determine the minimum rogue level required to flank the character.
classFeatures.name: Improved Uncanny Dodge
